t: If Δ₁=|[x b b; a x b; a a x]| and Δ₂=|[x b; a x]|, then
s:
Concept: 
To differentiate a determinant with respect to x, differentiate one row (or column) at a time while keeping the remaining rows unchanged, then add the resulting determinants. 

Calculation:
Δ₂ = |[x b; a x]| = x² - ab

Differentiating Δ₁ row-wise with respect to x:
d/dx(Δ₁) = |[1 0 0; a x b; a a x]| + |[x b b; 0 1 0; a a x]| + |[x b b; a x b; 0 0 1]|
Expanding each about the differentiated row:
d/dx(Δ₁) = (x² - ab) + (x² - ab) + (x² - ab)
d/dx(Δ₁) = 3(x² - ab) = 3Δ₂

Options (A), (C), and (D) are incorrect because Δ₁ is a degree-3 polynomial in x and Δ₂ is of degree 2; thus d/dx(Δ₁) has degree 2, ruling out Δ₂² (degree 4) and non-matching powers.

Correct Answer: (B) d/dx(Δ₁)=3Δ₂
